labels.label: cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd

hypotheses.paper: P(Γ) a property defined on cycles Γ (l.161)
hypotheses.note: Any P : ℤ → ℕ → Prop on pairs (x, n) with n ≥ 1 and T^[n] x = x. A property of the orbit, or one that fixes n as the least period, is a special case.

hypotheses.paper: the sign of the cycles Γ (OQ-63 (a))
hypotheses.note: Both forms are proved and no reading is chosen. Every cycle of ℤ is covered from theo:mr (…_mr, …_mr_aun, …_mr_alt and the effective forms). The positive cycles are covered from theo:matveev (…_matveev…), whose printed form needs 2^a > 3^b (finding 1).
A reading: ≤ C · 2^{|Γ|(1−ε)} with one constant C for all Γ (question 1).
A reading: p_n(x), the sum of a over one period (question 2).

The …_aun and …_alt forms carry the GCD of the printed A_u^n and of OQ-43's A'^n_u, for an n-periodic α with α(k + c) = a_k(x) for some shift c. That covers both index conventions (OQ-63 (b)). The GCD over one period is the GCD over ℤ (citedSteps_gcd_dvd). The …_mr and …_matveev forms (and their effective forms) assume less: a bound on |2^{p_n} − 3^n|, which is at most either GCD (citedSteps_abs_le_gcd).

hypotheses.paper: a Baker-type lower bound on |2^p − 3^n| (theo:mr l.145–148, theo:matveev l.156–159; the proof l.167 uses it unnamed)
hypotheses.note: Taken as the explicit hypothesis CitedStepsMR or CitedStepsMatveev, both stated as printed. It is never an axiom and never a named external; that is T-syr-cited's question. Neither is refuted in its elementary range: citedStepsMatveev_of_le covers a ≤ d, and citedStepsMR_of_lt covers a < 2^775.
A reading (question 4): an explicit bound B(C, ε) on |Γ|, and every P-cycle lies in the computable Finset citedStepsCandidates ⌊B⌋₊ (…_effective…).

findings: syracuse.tex:156–159 (theo:matveev), as used at l.302 and l.326 (« the corollary to Matveev Theorem »). As printed, theo:matveev assumes 2^a > 3^b, so it bounds |2^{p_n} − 3^n| only on positive cycles: on a cycle, 2^{p_n} − 3^n has the sign of x (two_pow_p_sub_three_pow_mul_pos). Over ℤ the corollary needs a bound for both signs, which theo:mr's form (l.145–148) gives. The corollary is proved over ℤ from theo:mr (property_defined_cycles_gcd_mr, _mr_aun, _mr_alt), and for the positive cycles from theo:matveev (property_defined_cycles_gcd_matveev, _aun, _alt). This bears on OQ-63 (a) and on § 3's negative cycles (−5, −7) and −17.

syracuse.tex:162: the GCD enters only through |2^{p_n} − 3^n|. On a cycle, that number divides every A_u^n and every A'^n_u, u ∈ ℤ, in every index convention (citedSteps_dvd_Aun), so it is at most either GCD (citedSteps_abs_le_gcd). For OQ-43's reading the GCD equals it (corGcdAlt_of_cycle). For the printed A_u^n the GCD is larger: 278 against 139 at −17 (citedSteps_gcd_instances). The corollary holds with the weaker hypothesis |2^{p_n} − 3^n| ≪ 2^{|Γ|(1−ε)}.

syracuse.tex:166–168: every step of the proof holds, and each is a theorem. First, n ≤ |Γ| (citedSteps_le_p). Second, |Γ| is bounded explicitly, through exp t ≥ t^{d+1}/(d+1)!: from theo:matveev, |Γ| ≤ C e^d (d+1)!/(ε log 2)^{d+1} (citedSteps_le_of_lower, citedSteps_le_of_matveev). From theo:mr, |Γ| ≤ max(2 log₂(2C)/ε, 2^800 log(3)^25 δ^25) with δ = max(1, 2/(ε log 2)) (citedSteps_le_of_mr). Third, a ranges over ⟦1, |Γ|⟧^n. Fourth, there is at most one cycle per a, because lem:base gives x(2^{p_n} − 3^n) = Σ_k 2^{p_k} 3^{n−1−k} (citedSteps_mul_eq_rhs, citedSteps_cycle_unique). Together: every cycle with p_n ≤ B lies in a computable Finset (mem_citedStepsCandidates), which the kernel evaluates on small B (citedStepsCandidates_decide). The proof does not say what bounds |Γ|; it is the cited lower bound printed just before (l.145–159), and l.190 says so in prose.

syracuse.tex:164, l.167: « effective » holds in principle, not in practice. theo:mr's conclusion is elementary for a < 2^775 (citedStepsMR_of_lt), so the bound it gives on |Γ| exceeds 2^800. theo:matveev's inequality is elementary for a ≤ d = 3.5·10^6 (citedStepsMatveev_of_le), and the bound it gives involves (d+1)!. The determination is a finite computation that cannot be carried out.

syracuse.tex:161–162, non-vacuity. With P = « two descending indices per period », the bound of T-syr-two-descents is the corollary's hypothesis (twoDesc_corollary_hyp, ε₀ ≈ 0.104, C = 2). So from theo:mr only finitely many cycles of ℤ qualify, and (−17, 7) is one (citedSteps_twoDesc_finite, citedSteps_twoDesc_neg_seventeen). With P = « one descending index per period », the bound of T-syr-steiner is the hypothesis on positive cycles (steiner_corollary_hypothesis). So from theo:matveev only finitely many positive cycles qualify, and (1, 1) is one (citedSteps_steiner_finite, citedSteps_steiner_one). TwoDescMatveev B, the hypothesis of theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited, follows from either cited bound at an explicit B (citedSteps_twoDescMatveev_of_matveev, citedSteps_twoDescMatveev_of_mr).
questions: « ≪ » (l.162). Reading taken: ≤ C · 2^{|Γ|(1−ε)}, with one constant C for all Γ (C may depend on P and ε). If C could depend on Γ, the hypothesis would always hold, and the corollary would claim finiteness for every P. That is false for pairs: (1, k), k ≥ 1. An « eventually » reading (|Γ| large) is equivalent, since there are finitely many cycles with bounded |Γ| (citedSteps_finite_of_le). It is not stated separately.
|Γ| (l.162). Reading taken: p_n(x) = Σ_{k<n} a_k(x), the sum over one period n, as T-syr-two-descents read l.323–324.

« cycles Γ » and « finitely many » (l.161–162). Reading taken: pairs (x, n) with n ≥ 1 and T^n x = x, and P any predicate on them. The conclusion is that the set of pairs is finite, which also bounds the points and the orbits.

« effective » (l.164, l.167). Reading taken: an explicit closed-form bound B(C, ε) on |Γ| (citedStepsBoundMR, citedStepsBoundMatveev), with every P-cycle in the computable list citedStepsCandidates ⌊B⌋₊. Deciding which candidates satisfy P needs P to be decidable, which the paper does not say. The computability of B as a real number is not formalized.
The sign of the cycles (OQ-63 (a)). Not ruled: both forms are proved, over ℤ from theo:mr and on the positive cycles from theo:matveev.

Which cited result the corollary rests on. Its proof (l.166–168) names none; its placement and l.302 / l.326 point to theo:matveev; only theo:mr covers both signs. Both are formalized, as alternative hypotheses, and the choice is left to T-syr-cited.
A_i in GCD(A_i(Γ) : i ∈ ℤ) (OQ-43, OQ-63 (b)). Both readings (Aun, AunAlt) and every index convention (a shift c) are covered. Nothing is chosen.
d = 3.5·10^6 in theo:matveev (l.159). Read as the integer 3500000, with e^d a^d = exp(d) · a^d.

labels.label: prop:proposition

hypotheses.paper: x ∈ ℤ, n ∈ ℕ*, T^n(x) = x
hypotheses.note: n is any period, not only the least one.

Carried in the printed form (prop_proposition_of_check, prop_proposition_of_cycleCheck). Weakened to x ≠ 1, with a strict inequality (prop_proposition_ne_one). Dropped for x < 0 (prop_proposition_neg). It cannot be dropped for x > 0 (prop_proposition_unbounded_false, at x = 1).

hypotheses.paper: the index convention of a_i in ⟦1, n⟧ (OQ-63 (b))
hypotheses.note: Both conventions give the same statement: on a cycle the count over ⟦1, n⟧ (l.62) equals the count over ⟦0, n−1⟧ (l.71), by citedStepsOnes_eq_range.

Used for x > 0 only, as the explicit hypothesis CitedStepsCheck: every odd 0 < y < 10^10 reaches 1 under T. The proof uses only its consequence CitedStepsCycleCheck: a positive cycle is (1) or lies above 10^10 (citedStepsCycleCheck_of_check). It is never an axiom; how it enters is T-syr-cited's question.
Used in its true form, Syracuse.bounds (strict, proved), which needs no hypothesis (prop_proposition_min). The printed cor:bounds is false (OQ-54 (c)). OQ-54 decides that row's mark, not this one.

findings: syracuse.tex:194–199: for x < 0 the statement holds unconditionally, with no computer check and no |x| > 1000: #{a_i = 1} > (2 − log₂3) n > α n (prop_proposition_neg). On a negative cycle 2^{p_n} < 3^n, so p_n < n log₂3, and p_n ≥ a + 2(n − a) (citedSteps_two_mul_le). This confirms the planner's [r]. At −1, at −5 and −7 (the two points of (−5, −7)) and at −17 the counts are 1, 1, 1 and 5, each above α n (prop_proposition_instances).

syracuse.tex:201: the inference « |x| > 10^{10} » holds only for x > 0. The tested « conjecture » is false over the negative integers (the cycles (−1), (−5, −7), (−17, …)), so the check says nothing about negative cycles. The gap is harmless, by the previous finding.

syracuse.tex:201–204: two slips in the proof, both harmless. First, it cites cor:bounds, which is false as printed (OQ-54 (c)). The true form gives #{a_i = 1} ≥ n(2 − log₂3 − log₂(1 + 1/(3 min))) on every cycle of ℤ* (prop_proposition_min). Second, l.202 and l.204 write log, which is the natural logarithm elsewhere in the paper (l.114), where cor:bounds has log₂. Once every point exceeds 10^{10}, log₂(1 + 1/(3·10^{10})) < 10^{−10} (prop_proposition_pos_of_ge), so the conclusion stands for x > 0, given the check (prop_proposition_of_check).

syracuse.tex:195: given the check, the hypothesis |x| > 1000 can be weakened to x ≠ 1, and the inequality becomes strict (prop_proposition_ne_one). It cannot be dropped: at the cycle (1) the count is 0 < α (prop_proposition_unbounded_false). No known cycle of ℤ has |x| > 1000, so the printed hypothesis is met by no known cycle.

syracuse.tex:197: α = 2 − log₂3 − 10^{−10} > 0.415037499 holds (citedStepsAlpha_gt), from 3^{79335} < 2^{125743} checked by decide in the kernel (citedSteps_logb_lt; 125743/79335 is a convergent of log₂3 from above). The margin is about 1.8·10^{−10}.
questions: The check of l.201. Reading taken: every odd y with 0 < y < 10^{10} reaches 1 under T (CitedStepsCheck). « integers » is read as positive integers, since the conjecture is false over the negatives. « no cycles have been found containing an integer bigger than 1000 » is read as part of the same check. The proof uses only the consequence CitedStepsCycleCheck. Whether the check becomes a named external, a hypothesis, or a kernel computation is T-syr-cited's question; a kernel computation up to 10^{10} is out of reach.
The index convention of a_i in ⟦1, n⟧ (OQ-63 (b)). Both are covered and the counts are equal on a cycle (citedStepsOnes_eq_range). Nothing is chosen.
log in l.202 and l.204. Read as log₂, the base cor:bounds uses. The step holds with either base.
n (l.194). Read as any n ≥ 1 with T^n x = x, not only the least period. The statement holds for every such n.
The sign of x (OQ-63 (a)). The statement says x ∈ ℤ, so both signs are proved: x < 0 unconditionally, x > 0 from the check.

kb_proposals: 3^q < 2^p with q ≈ 8·10^4 closes by decide in the kernel in under a second, under `set_option exponentiation.threshold 200000 in`. Then exact_mod_cast to ℝ, Real.log_lt_log and Real.log_pow give logb 2 3 < p/q (citedSteps_logb_lt). Take a convergent of log₂3 from above (125743/79335 gives a precision of about 10^{-10}).

Finiteness of cycles. Every cycle (x, n) of ℤ with p_n ≤ B lies in the computable Finset citedStepsCandidates B, because lem:base fixes x from a (mem_citedStepsCandidates). Set.Finite.subset of its coercion gives finiteness. Small memberships close by decide, one per decide: a conjunction of three hit maxRecDepth.
At literal (x, n, B), call mem_citedStepsCandidates with (x := …) (n := …) (B := …) explicitly. Otherwise elaboration hits maxRecDepth.

From a Baker-type lower bound to a bound on P: Real.pow_div_factorial_le_exp (exp t ≥ t^{d+1}/(d+1)!) turns 2^{Pε} ≤ C K P^d into P ≤ C K (d+1)!/(ε log 2)^{d+1} (citedSteps_le_of_lower). For a bound on |a log 2 − b log 3| (theo:mr's form), use |log u| ≤ 2|1 − u| when |1 − u| ≤ 1/2 (citedSteps_abs_log_le).
Real.log_two_gt_d9 lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds, which Syracuse does not import. For log 2 ≥ 1/2 and log 3 ≥ 1/2, use Real.one_sub_inv_le_log_of_pos, which needs no new import.
To equate aPer n x with an explicit periodic sequence, use citedSteps_periodic_ext with aPer_natCast (for example aPer 7 (−17) = seq17). After that, decide evaluates counts and GCDs.
notes: Nothing is marked: both rows are partial and wait on T-syr-cited, and where they bear, on OQ-63 (a) and OQ-54 (c). There is no axiom, no named external and no sorry. #print axioms on each of the 64 declarations shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (citedStepsD and citedStepsExt depend on none). There is no native_decide. The cited inputs are four Prop-valued defs that appear as hypotheses of the theorems: CitedStepsMR (theo:mr as printed), CitedStepsMatveev (theo:matveev as printed), CitedStepsCheck (l.201) and its consequence CitedStepsCycleCheck. T-syr-cited's ruling would name them or discharge them. TwoDescMatveev B of the strict TwoDescents.lean already follows from either bound at an explicit B (citedSteps_twoDescMatveev_of_matveev, citedSteps_twoDescMatveev_of_mr). The file imports only Syracuse.TwoDescents and Syracuse.Steiner; there is no new Mathlib import. It is not added to scaffold/SyracuseScaffold.lean or to Syracuse.lean. The one `lake build SyracuseScaffold.CitedSteps`, run last, after checking that no other build was running, built only this module (2190 jobs, nothing upstream rebuilt) and gave no warning. The file is written for the strict library: it typechecks under lake env lean with no warning and no deprecated tactic. Docstring lines over 100 characters are table rows and the verbatim TeX quote, as in TwoDescents.lean. Names: helpers are prefixed citedSteps / CitedSteps, and label theorems are property_defined_cycles_gcd_* and prop_proposition_*. There is no clash with the strict Syracuse.*. NoCircuit.lean (T-syr-no-circuit) was not read, as the dispatch requires, so clashes with it must be checked at graduation. The docstring has no ``**`label`**`` anywhere (ledger regex checked). Both labels appear with syracuse.tex lines in the first 300 characters, and the quotes were checked verbatim against legacy/labeled/syracuse.tex.
